definitions: A measure used in various fields (e.g., economics, engineering, medicine) to quantify the relationship between the lowest point (trough) and the highest point (peak) of a fluctuating variable or series.
The quotient obtained by dividing the minimum value by the maximum value within a specified period or cycle.
examples: The Trough-to-Peak ratio indicated market volatility.
Engineers analyzed the Trough-to-Peak ratio of the signal.
Physicians monitored the Trough-to-Peak ratio of drug concentration.
